questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher will / certainly help you / if you will / ask her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In conditional sentences, the word **"if"** is followed by the **simple present tense, not "will".**
 
• The correct phrase should be** "if you ask her,"** ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

**Correct Sentence: *"The teacher will certainly help you if you ask her.__"***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "ask her," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "The teacher will,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "certainly help you,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 2.

My Vice-Chancellor works / eighteen hours / a day, / seven days week.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the article "**a**" before the term "**week**."
 
• Singular countable nouns typically require an article** ("a" or "an").**

• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"My Vice-Chancellor works eighteen hours a day, seven days a week.__"***

• **Option 3: "eighteen hours"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "a day"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the verb "**picks**" which should be in the base form to match the subject "**I**."
 
• The correct form of the verb should be "**pick**" to agree with the subject "I" in the present simple tense.
 
• The correct sentence should be "**Between two evils, I always pick the one I have never tried before**" ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

• The primary issue in the sentence is **the inconsistency in verb tense.**
 
• The phrase "**It was possible**" is in the past tense, while the phrase "**if one has**" is in the present tense.

• Thus, the error is located in **part A** of the sentence.

**Correct Sentence:** ***"It is possible to achieve anything, if one has the grit and determination to keep going."***

• The word "**principle**" refers to** a fundamental truth or proposition that serves as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.**
 
• "**Profit**" refers to **the financial gain made in a transaction.**
 
• The other options do not correctly fit the context of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

• Understanding the context of the sentence helps in choosing the correct homophones.

• **Example: **Industrial waste can **contaminate** water sources, making them unsafe for drinking.

• **Example: **To ensure safe drinking water, it is essential to** purify** it by removing harmful substances.

• **Example:** She** requested** extra time to complete the project.
 
 
 
• **Discovered** (खोजा): To find something or someone unexpectedly or during a search.
 
 
• **Example: **The scientist **discovered** a new species of plant.
 
 
 
• **System** (प्रणाली): A set of connected things or parts forming a complex whole.
